## 4. What the registry cannot express

The most useful section for deciding what to build next: concepts a real obligation
has that **no field on `ObligationRule` can carry**. Written from the type, not from
any one obligation.

★ Each gap below is machine-guarded. If a future field closes one, the export script
throws instead of emitting a document that states a gap which no longer exists.

### A window of N days AFTER the deadline

Nothing on a rule expresses "late, but still inside a remediation window". The REQ has one (art. 73, 60 days) and the roster update has one (art. 41, 30 days). `deadlineDays` is the opposite thing — an offset from a triggering ACT to the deadline, used by event-cadence rules. NOTE: `LivenessInput` already declares `legalWindowDays`, and computeLiveness never reads it.

### Escalation on the NUMBER of occurrences in default

Nothing counts instances. A second missed filing carries a different consequence from a first, and that is a property of the COMPANY, not of a row. A rule is evaluated per obligation, so no field on this type can hold it — it would have to be computed across rows and injected.

### A dueDate that depends on a FILING REGIME

`dueDate` is a function and can branch, but `ObligationDueCtx` carries only fyEnd, immatriculationDate, incorporationDate, fiscalYears and today. Nothing says which regime applies to this company, so a rule with two lawful deadlines cannot choose between them.

### Extinction — an obligation that stops applying

No rule can declare that it ceases to apply (superseded, absorbed by a later period, no longer owed). Today the only mechanism is `exempt_from_lateness`, a CATALOG column read by the completeness engine — decided outside the registry, and invisible to a rule.

### A severity distinct from the liveness tier

A rule cannot say how BAD a default is. The liveness axis answers "can the user still fix this alone?" and rank.ts answers "how urgent?" — neither answers "what is the consequence?". A fine and a dissolution currently carry the same tier.
